content:
*Functional Programming in Lean* is a free online book that introduces functional programming using Lean 4. It is intended for readers who know how to program, but who have never used a functional language. If you do have experience with Haskell, OCaml, Racket, Scala, or PureScript, then some aspects of the book may move a bit slowly for your taste.

If you follow along on this site, you may have seen a series of announcements of prereleases as I've been working on the text. This is no prerelease - the book is done! It's just over 118 thousand words.

The source code for the book is now public. I'll be fixing mistakes from time to time, and making as much an effort as time allows to keep it up to date with the latest releases of Lean 4. I'm not interested in pull requests, however - the support code serves its purpose, and I consider the text to be a single-author project with a consistent voice. If you really think I'd like your PR, please get in touch first so that you don't waste effort.

I'd like to thank you all for the warm reception I've received here, for the careful comments from readers, and for help when I was having a hard time understanding Lean 4. Please see the Acknowledgments section for a more precise list of names. I'd also like to thank Microsoft Research for their financial support and technical assistance, without which this project could never have been completed, and Leo for suggesting it in the first place.
